items.t: Sardis is a Chilliwack neighbourhood south of Highway 1 and the Vedder River, under the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, Schedule B5 of the 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP).
The plan borders it with Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) land west and east, First Nations lands south and east, and Vedder south.
Vedder Road is the corridor plans use to divide east and west Sardis.
Garrison Crossing (Tamihi Way, Market Way, Chehalis Drive) is in east Sardis; Promontory is its southeast hillside.
Older streets east of Vedder Road use R1-A and R3: R3 (Small Lot Residential) sets a 360-square-metre minimum lot, 12-metre width, and permits an accessory dwelling unit.
Garrison Crossing houses use CD-9: minimum lots of 240 square metres detached, 480 duplex, 9-metre width.
West of Vedder Road, West Evans, between Stevenson Road and Evans Road, is ALR along the urban boundary.
Promontory-edge houses use HR (Hillside Residential): 0.2-hectare minimum lot with community water.

blocks.text: Sardis Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Sardis sits on the Vedder River alluvial fan, and the OCP's fan permit area covers Sardis, including Garrison Crossing.
Floodplain Regulation Bylaw 2018, No. 4519 designates the Vedder floodplain and fans as floodplain; the setback is 75 metres from the Vedder River's natural boundary.

blocks.text: Sardis Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Sardis Park, 6898 School Lane: 5-hectare former gravel pit with a pond and 655-metre loop.
Sardis Library, 5819 Tyson Road, sits beside Sardis Sports Complex, 5725 Tyson Road (three rinks).
Cheam Leisure Centre, 45501 Market Way, is Sardis's leisure centre.
Grocery anchors: Save-On-Foods Sardis, 6014 Vedder Road; Save-On-Foods Garrison, 45635 Tamihi Way.

blocks.text: Sardis Houses: development and new projects

items.t: Sardis Secondary addition, 45460 Stevenson Road: mass timber addition by School District No. 33 and the Province, 400 seats, capacity 1,600. STATUS: completed August 2026, confirmed by the district October 1, 2026, read 2026-11-03.

Promontory elementary site, 5303 Promontory Road: the district board approved buying this property for a future elementary school. STATUS: land purchased; ministry approvals and funding still required, read 2026-11-03.
South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan: plan in preparation for southeast Vedder below Promontory, beside Tzeachten First Nation. STATUS: in preparation, read 2026-11-03.
Andmar: see sardis-condos-for-sale. Keith Wilson: see sardis-townhomes-for-sale.
City-wide 2026 rates and charges apply in Sardis: see chilliwack-houses-for-sale.
Houses on Tzeachten and Skowkale reserve land named in the plan sit outside the City tax roll and outside Speculation and Vacancy Tax areas, per the Province.
Route 51 Vedder: Vedder Road, University of the Fraser Valley campus to Downtown Chilliwack, via Vedder/Promontory and Vedder/Luckakuck.
Route 52 Evans: Chilliwack to Cottonwood Mall via Evans Road, serving west Sardis.

blocks.text: Sardis Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check lots on City floodplain maps: Bylaw No. 4519's fan designation covers Sardis broadly, not only riverfront lots.
Promontory-edge lots: Development Permit Area 2 requires a geotechnical report before building or clearing.

faq.a: It depends on the middle school. The District No. 33 locator for 45501 Market Way returned Watson Elementary, then a choice of Mount Slesse or Vedder Middle, then G.W. Graham or Sardis Secondary matching that choice. Run the exact address.

Most of Sardis sits on the Vedder River alluvial fan. The OCP carries a permit area for the fan, and Bylaw No. 4519 designates the fan as floodplain, with a 75-metre setback and floors set by the flood construction level.
faq.q: Is a Sardis house on a flood fan?

faq.a: They were built under one comprehensive zone, CD-9, not the standard R1-A or R3 zones. CD-9 sets minimums — 240 square metres for a detached house lot, 170 for a rowhouse — and allows townhouse and apartment forms under R4 and R5 standards.
faq.q: How are Garrison Crossing houses different?

faq.a: Yes, on small-lot streets: R3 lists an accessory dwelling unit as a permitted ancillary use. Check the flood design first, because fan rules apply there.
